path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]
Deduction of tax at source on benefit or perquisite in respect of business or profession [Section 194R]

exclusion: benefits or perquisites to a resident where aggregate value does not exceed 20,000 rupees in a financial year
providers being individuals or HUFs whose business turnover or professional receipts do not exceed statutory thresholds
inclusion: benefits or perquisites arising from business or exercise of a profession
perquisites provided wholly in kind, partly in kind, or in cash
descriptor.definition: Any person providing business or professional benefits or perquisites to a resident must ensure tax is deducted at source before release, regardless of whether the benefit is in cash, kind, or partly both. If the benefit is wholly or partly in kind and available cash is insufficient to cover tax, the deductor must ensure tax is paid prior to release.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard monetary income TDS by capturing non-monetary or mixed business advantages provided to trade partners or professionals.

path.name: Chapter 2: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS)
Unit 5: THE ELEMENTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
LINK BETWEEN INFORMATION IN GENERAL PURPOSE FINANCIAL REPORTS AS PER CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK AND ELEMENTS OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
Link Between Information In General Purpose Financial Reports As Per Conceptual Framework And Elements Of Financial Statements

exclusion: Equity contributions and distributions categorized as financial performance elements
inclusion: Mapping of economic resources to assets and claims to liabilities
Mapping of financial changes to income and expense elements
descriptor.definition: General purpose financial reports reflect underlying economic resources and claims through specific balance sheet elements like assets, liabilities, and equity. Changes in these resources and claims over time are captured via financial performance elements such as income and expenses.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes static structural elements (assets, liabilities, equity) from dynamic performance elements (income, expenses).

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Capital receipts generally excluded from business income computations
inclusion: Profits realized in cash or in kind
Single trade ventures if undertaken with profit intent
Vocations included under professional scope
descriptor.definition: Business encompasses trade, commerce, manufacture, or any trade adventure pursued with a profit motive, whereas profession denotes occupations requiring specialized learning and includes vocations. Profits from both categories are generally taxable under the same head, while differences persist primarily for tax audit and presumptive taxation thresholds.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between continuous commercial operations and isolated trade adventures, and differentiates traditional businesses from learned professions.

exclusion: Non-residents unless specific conditions apply
inclusion: Companies
Firms
Resident individuals holding foreign assets or financial interests
descriptor.definition: A return of income is a formal declaration furnished by an assessee detailing total income, deductions, and tax payable in a prescribed format. Companies and firms must file it compulsorily, along with specific resident individuals holding foreign assets or signing authorities.
nearby_distinctions: Differs from a return of loss or revised return by being the primary mandatory periodic filing of taxable income under regular provisions.

exclusion: Original receipts that never received prior expense or loss write-off deductions
inclusion: Subsequent cash receipts compensating for prior allowed losses or expenditures
Benefits derived from previously written-off trading liabilities
descriptor.definition: Recoveries or benefits derived from previously allowed deductions for losses, expenditures, or trading liabilities are treated as taxable income. This deemed income is taxable in the financial year in which the amount is received or the benefit accrues.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary income generation events from secondary recoveries of previously claimed expense deductions.

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 3: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

exclusion: Financial service providers from corporate person definition
inclusion: Financial debt
Operational debt
Secured and unsecured creditors
descriptor.definition: Statutory definitions under the code establish key regulatory terms including the governing board, corporate person status, claims, and debts. These provisions outline the precise legal boundaries for creditors, charges, and financial or operational obligations.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between financial debts disbursed for time value of money and general operational claims.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
CERTAIN SUMS DEEMED AS PROFITS AND GAINS OF BUSINESS OR PROFESSION [SECTION 38]
Certain Sums Deemed As Profits And Gains Of Business Or Profession [Section 38]

exclusion: Receipts unrelated to prior business deductions or allowances
inclusion: Unilateral write-offs of trading liabilities in accounts
Benefits or cash obtained from previously allowed losses or expenditures
Tax liability transferred to business successors like amalgamated or resulting companies
descriptor.definition: Specific receipts such as the remission or cessation of a previously deducted trading liability are statutorily deemed as business profits. These amounts remain taxable even if the underlying business has ceased to exist or has been transferred to a successor.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes normal revenue receipts from recovered deductions or remitted liabilities deemed as taxable business profits.

path.name: Chapter 19: Professional Ethics & Liabilities of Auditors
Allowing Unqualified Persons to Practice in Accountant Name

exclusion: Allowing non-chartered accountants or relatives lacking qualifications to practice under the member's name
inclusion: Permitting qualified partners to practice in the member's name
Permitting firm employees to practice in the member's name
descriptor.definition: A practicing chartered accountant commits professional misconduct by permitting any unqualified person to practice under their name. However, partners who are qualified chartered accountants in practice or firm employees may practice under that name.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between permitted use of a CA firm name by qualified internal partners or employees versus prohibited use by external unqualified individuals.
instrument_references: Clause (1) of Part I of the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Case study Facts of the case
Auditor Accountability for Related Party Transactions

exclusion: Arm's length transactions conducted entirely with unrelated third-party customers in the open market
inclusion: Evaluation of sales transactions executed with entities connected to director family members
Review of missing documentation supporting related party transaction pricing
Initiation of disciplinary action for deficient audit working papers
descriptor.definition: Examines engagement partner liability regarding the validation of arm's length pricing and documentation for transactions executed with related corporate parties. Auditors must critically evaluate significant commercial dealings with entities connected to key managerial personnel to ensure complete transparency and compliance.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general revenue verification by requiring explicit scrutiny of ownership ties and pricing justifications between the reporting entity and insiders.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
CERTAIN DEDUCTIONS ALLOWED ON ACTUAL PAYMENT BASIS ONLY [SECTION 37]
Certain Deductions Allowed On Actual Payment Basis Only [Section 37]

exclusion: Expenses claimable purely on accrual without regard to actual payment mandates
inclusion: Taxes, duties, cess, or fees levied under law
Employer contributions to provident, superannuation, or gratuity funds
Bonus, commission, or leave encashment payable to employees
descriptor.definition: Specific statutory liabilities such as taxes, duties, welfare fund contributions, leave encashment, and bonuses are deductible only upon actual payment regardless of accounting methods. However, timely payments made on or before the return filing due date fulfill this condition for the incurred tax year.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard accrual-based commercial expenses from statutory liabilities requiring actual cash outflow or timely return-filing payment.

path.name: Residuary Scope of Income from Other Sources

exclusion: Income specifically falling under salaries, house property, business or profession, or capital gains
inclusion: Receipts failing to fall under other specific heads of income
Profits and gains not covered elsewhere
descriptor.definition: Income from other sources functions as a residuary tax head capturing all taxable profits, gains, or receipts that fail to qualify under any preceding specific head. It applies to any item chargeable under the Act that does not find a precise classification within other established income categories.
nearby_distinctions: Unlike specific heads with strict categorization criteria, this acts as a catch-all for remaining taxable items.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Rental income from letting out residential houses by the owner
inclusion: Active business or professional earnings carried on during the tax year
descriptor.definition: Profits and gains arising from any business or profession carried on by the assessee during the tax year are chargeable under this head. Rental income generated by an owner from letting out a residential house is specifically taxable under house property income rather than business profits.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes commercial leasing objectives from residential house property rentals governed by specific statutory classifications.

exclusion: Fundamental company valuation metrics
Qualitative management capability assessments
inclusion: Calculation of n-period arithmetic moving averages
Computation of exponential moving averages using a smoothing constant
Identification of short, intermediate, and long-term trends
descriptor.definition: Chartists analyze price data using moving averages to generate buy and sell signals based on trend identification over specified time horizons. Arithmetic moving averages apply equal weights to past prices, while exponential moving averages assign exponentially decreasing weights starting with the latest price.
nearby_distinctions: Arithmetic moving averages treat all periods within the lookback equally, whereas exponential moving averages weight recent prices more heavily.

path.name: Chapter 19: Provisions to Counteract Unethical Tax Practices
Penalties for Foreign Income and Asset Non-Compliance

exclusion: Low-value bank accounts and minor aggregate asset holdings within statutory monetary limits
inclusion: Penalties equal to three times the tax computed
Fixed sum penalties for omission of foreign asset information
descriptor.definition: Assessees face financial penalties amounting to multiples of computed tax or fixed monetary fines for failing to disclose foreign assets or file required returns. Specific monetary thresholds and asset types provide exemptions from these penalties under defined conditions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinct from prosecution as these represent administrative financial sanctions rather than criminal imprisonment offenses.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
SPECIAL PROVISION FOR COMPUTING PROFITS AND GAINS OF BUSINESS OR PROFESSION ON PRESUMPTIVE BASIS IN CASE OF CERTAIN RESIDENTS [SECTION 58]

exclusion: Assessees claiming specific deductions under Chapter VIII Part C
inclusion: Resident individuals, HUFs, and partnership firms excluding LLPs
Businesses with turnover up to 2 crores or 3 crores subject to cash transaction limits
descriptor.definition: Eligible resident taxpayers engaged in specified businesses with turnover below statutory limits can compute their business profits using pre-determined presumptive rates. The taxable profit is calculated based on percentages of turnover received via specified digital modes versus cash.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from normal computation provisions by eliminating the need to maintain detailed expense records if statutory profit margins are met.

path.name: Chapter 6: Ind AS on Liabilities of the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 37: PROVISIONS, CONTINGENT LIABILITIES AND CONTINGENT ASSETS
Scope of Appendix C of Ind AS 37

exclusion: Subsequent cost accounting arising from levy recognition
inclusion: Liabilities to pay government levies with certain timing and amounts
descriptor.definition: Appendix C specifies accounting treatment for levy liabilities falling under Ind AS 37 when their timing and amount are certain. It explicitly omits the subsequent cost accounting arising from recognizing such levy liabilities.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct levy liability accounting from the accounting treatment applied to resulting asset or expense costs.

path.name: Chapter 8: Ind AS on Disclosures in the Financial Statements
Understanding relationship between the reporting entity and another entity/entities
Relationship Between Reporting Entity and Other Entities

exclusion: Entities linked merely by a shared common director without additional control or significant influence
inclusion: Fellow subsidiaries and group parents
Joint ventures and associates
Post-employment benefit plans for employees
descriptor.definition: An entity is related to a reporting entity if they are group members, associates, joint ventures, or controlled by the same person. Additional links include post-employment benefit plans and entities providing key management personnel services.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes structural corporate affiliations and shared control frameworks from casual operational partnerships.

path.name: CAPITAL GAINS IN RESPECT OF SLUMP SALE [SECTION 77]
Capital Gains in Respect of Slump Sale

exclusion: Transfer of individual assets or liabilities not constituting an active business undertaking
inclusion: Transfer of an entire undertaking, division, or business activity for a lump sum
Assets held for more than 36 months taxed as long-term and 36 months or less as short-term
descriptor.definition: A slump sale involves transferring one or more undertakings for a lump sum consideration without assigning values to individual assets and liabilities. The net worth of the undertaking is deemed the cost of acquisition and improvement, while the fair market value serves as the full value of consideration.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from itemized asset sales because individual asset valuation is absent, utilizing undertaking net worth instead.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
AMOUNTS NOT DEDUCTIBLE IN CERTAIN CIRCUMSTANCES [SECTION 35]
Amounts Not Deductible In Certain Circumstances [Section 35]

exclusion: Taxes where statutory relief or exemptions apply without business deduction eligibility
inclusion: Income tax and foreign tax payments eligible for relief
Employer-paid tax on non-monetary employee perquisites
Thirty percent disallowance for resident payments lacking required tax deduction or timely deposit
descriptor.definition: Certain expenditures such as income taxes, foreign taxes eligible for relief, and employer-paid taxes on non-monetary employee perquisites are disallowed as deductions. Furthermore, a specified percentage of sums payable to residents is disallowed if tax deduction at source requirements and subsequent payment timelines are defaulted.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard deductible operating business expenses from statutory disallowances imposed due to tax compliance failures.

path.name: Chapter 19: Provisions to Counteract Unethical Tax Practices
OVERVIEW OF THE BLACK MONEY & IMPOSITION OF TAX LAW
Black Money and Imposition of Tax Framework

exclusion: Domestic undisclosed income governed solely by standard domestic tax codes without foreign elements
inclusion: Undisclosed income from foreign sources
Undisclosed assets located abroad
descriptor.definition: The framework establishes stringent taxation on undisclosed foreign income and assets held by individuals. It aims to deter and penalize foreign assets accumulated outside the country without proper tax disclosures.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard domestic tax evasion provisions by its specific focus on extraterritorial assets and distinct penalty structures.
instrument_references: The Black Money and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015

path.name: Chapter 7: Ind AS on Items impacting the Financial Statements
Unit 2: INDIAN ACCOUNTING STANDARD 21 : THE EFFECTS OF CHANGES IN FOREIGN

exclusion: Hedge accounting for foreign currency items and net investment hedging
Statement of cash flows presentation of foreign currency cash flows
Long term foreign currency monetary items utilizing Ind AS 101 exemptions
inclusion: Foreign currency derivatives not covered by Ind AS 109
Translation of results and financial position of foreign operations
Translation into presentation currency
descriptor.definition: The standard applies to accounting for foreign currency transactions, foreign operations consolidation, and translating financial statements into presentation currency. It explicitly excludes specific areas like hedge accounting, cash flow statements, and specific long-term monetary item exemptions.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard foreign currency translation rules from specialised treatments governed separately by Ind AS 109, Ind AS 7, and Ind AS 101.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: employer-paid tax on non-monetary perquisites
tax deducted under section 194N on cash withdrawals
inclusion: all sums deducted under Chapter XVII TDS provisions
eligible foreign income tax deductions allowed as credit
descriptor.definition: All taxes deducted under statutory provisions and eligible foreign tax deductions are treated as income received when computing an assessee's total income. Specific statutory outflows, such as non-monetary perquisite taxes paid by employers and certain cash withdrawal deductions, are excluded from this income-inclusion rule.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from gross cash receipts by legally mandating the addition of withheld tax amounts back into the taxpayer's computed income base.

path.name: Chapter 9: Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers”

exclusion: Procedural guidance for step execution
inclusion: Standardized accounting definitions for revenue recognition mechanics
descriptor.definition: This section sets out foundational terminology used throughout the revenue standard, including contracts, contract assets, contract liabilities, and performance obligations. These terms provide the technical definitions required to execute the five-step revenue recognition model.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between contract assets conditioned on factors other than the passage of time versus unconditional rights to consideration.

exclusion: Incomes explicitly exempt from charge under statutory provisions
inclusion: Total income of persons specified under the Act
Tax rates specified by the Finance Act or Income-tax Act, 2025
descriptor.definition: Income-tax is charged on the total income of every person for the tax year at the rates prescribed by the annual Finance Act or the Income-tax Act, 2025. This charging provision forms the foundational basis from which any tax liability legally originates.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from computational provisions by serving strictly as the legal origin of tax liability.

path.name: Chapter 5: Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements

exclusion: interest expense recognized over credit period
costs incurred after cessation of capitalization
inclusion: cash price equivalent for deferred payments
costs of testing whether the asset works properly

Capitalization ceases once the asset is capable of operating in the manner intended by management.
nearby_distinctions: Separate acquisition cost components versus business combination fair value measurement

path.name: IBS source reference: SPOM Set A
Chapter 1: Appointment and Qualification of Directors

exclusion: Private companies lacking public company listing or financial threshold triggers
Mandatory appointments when financial conditions fail to be met for three consecutive years
inclusion: One-third independent director quota for listed public companies
Minimum of two independent directors for unlisted public companies meeting financial thresholds
Mandatory filling of intermittent vacancies by the next board meeting or three months
descriptor.definition: Listed public companies must maintain at least one-third of their total directors as independent directors, while specific classes of unlisted public companies must appoint a minimum of two based on paid-up capital, turnover, or loan thresholds. Intermittent vacancies must be filled within specified statutory timeframes.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from executive or non-executive ordinary directors by strict statutory independence criteria and quantitative financial scale triggers.

path.name: Chapter 20: Tax Audit and Ethical Compliances
Mandatory Tax Audit Provisions and Thresholds

exclusion: Assessees declaring profits in accordance with section 44AD(1) or 44ADA(1)
inclusion: Businesses with total sales exceeding specific statutory limits
Professions with gross receipts exceeding fifty lakh rupees
Assessees claiming lower profits than presumptive rates under designated sections
descriptor.definition: Certain businesses and professions must get their accounts audited by a chartered accountant before the specified date when financial metrics cross prescribed monetary thresholds. Exceptions and specific conditions regarding cash receipts and payments apply to business turnovers within defined limits.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes business turnover thresholds from professional gross receipt thresholds and presumptive income reporting rules.

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
Credit for tax deducted at source [Section 199]
Credit For Tax Deducted At Source [Section 199]

exclusion: Direct payment of tax without statutory deduction mechanism
Credit given without matching deductor information
inclusion: Credit given to the deductee based on deductor reporting

path.name: Chapter 13: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax

exclusion: insurance commission
professional services
inclusion: payments for services rendered in the course of buying or selling goods
transactions relating to assets or valuable articles other than securities

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Liabilities or portions met directly or indirectly by other persons or authorities
inclusion: Adjustments to asset costs due to exchange rate variations upon payment
Gains or losses on foreign currency transactions computed via notified standards

Separately, general gains or losses from foreign currency transactions are computed in accordance with notified standards.

path.name: Chapter 19: Professional Ethics & Liabilities of Auditors
Disabilities for the Purpose of Membership
Disabilities for the Purpose of Membership

exclusion: General register maintenance
Certificate of practice requirements
inclusion: Age and mental capacity criteria
Insolvency and criminal conviction conditions
Removal from membership consequences
descriptor.definition: Section 8 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949 outlines specific legal conditions that prevent individuals from being registered or retaining membership. Disqualifications include minority age, unsound mind, insolvency, conviction for moral turpitude, or prior removal for professional misconduct.
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes permanent or conditional legal disqualifications from standard fee-based removal provisions.
instrument_references: Section 8 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
Section 5 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949

exclusion: Legitimate business or earning expenditures properly subjected to tax withholding requirements
inclusion: Personal expenses of the assessee
Payments exceeding specified limits made via non-banking channels
Thirty percent of resident sums subject to TDS left unpaid by the return due date
descriptor.definition: Certain expenditures are barred from deduction when computing income under this head, including personal expenses, un-deducted overseas interest, and salaries paid abroad without tax deduction. Additional restrictions apply to excessive payments to related parties, transactions exceeding cash limits, and unpaid resident sums subject to tax deduction at source.

path.name: Chapter 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession

exclusion: Taxpayers not meeting statutory income or turnover thresholds and not carrying on specified professions
inclusion: Specified professions like legal, medical, and engineering
Businesses exceeding specified income or turnover limits in preceding years

These records can be kept in written, electronic, digital, cloud-based, or printed formats.

path.name: Chapter 2: Incomes which do not form part of Total Income
RESTRICTIONS ON ALLOWABILITY OF EXPENDITURE [SECTION 14 READ WITH RULE 14]

exclusion: Expenditures incurred solely in relation to taxable income streams
inclusion: Direct expenditure relating to exempt income
Indirect expenditure computed as a percentage of investment balances under prescribed rules

exclusion: Ordinary colloquial meanings where statutory definitions explicitly expand or restrict terms
